core_meaning.primary_meaning: David (Hebrew דָּוִד, Dāwiḏ) is a masculine name of Hebrew origin meaning “beloved”. Its popularity comes from King David, the shepherd who killed Goliath and became the second king of the united Kingdom of Israel, a central figure in Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The name is linked to the Hebrew root dôwd (דּוֹד), which in Biblical Hebrew survives in the figurative sense “to love”; as a noun dod means “uncle” and, poetically, “beloved” — as in the Song of Songs 6:3, “I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine”.

etymology.morphology: Personal name related to the noun dod, “uncle; beloved”.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From Hebrew דָּוִד, linked to the root dôwd, whose Biblical Hebrew sense is “to love”; dod also means “uncle” and “beloved”.

origin.origin_explanation: Hebrew, from the Bible. Christians adopted it early — Greek Δαυίδ, Latin David, Syriac Dawid — and the Qur'anic form is Dāwūd.

religion.religious_status: Name of King David of the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament
religion.religious_explanation: In the Books of Samuel David is a young shepherd and harpist who kills the Philistine Goliath, later becomes king of Judah and then of all Israel, and makes Jerusalem his capital. The Book of Samuel calls him “the sweet psalmist of Israel”, and almost half of the Psalms carry the heading “A Psalm of David”. In the New Testament Jesus is called the Son of David.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: Saint David (6th century) is the patron saint of Wales, where the name also takes the form Dafydd.
cultural_context.impact: Name days fall on 1 March for St David of Wales and 29 December for King David.

pronunciation.note: Modern Hebrew says da-VEED; Welsh Dafydd is DAH-vith.

name_variants.variant_notes: Dafydd is Welsh, Davide Italian, Dawud/Dāwūd the Arabic and Qur'anic form; Dave and Davy are short forms.

known_linguistic_history: King David's reign is placed around the 9th–10th century BC by the biblical account.
Adopted as a Christian name from an early period, e.g. David of Wales (6th century) and David I of Iberia.
historical_context.historical_person_association: King David, second king of the united Kingdom of Israel.

modern_usage.modern_context: A classic name across Europe and the English-speaking world; Dave and Davy are its common short forms.

faq.a: In the Hebrew Bible David is the shepherd who killed Goliath and became the second king of the united Kingdom of Israel, with Jerusalem as his capital.
Yes — in 1 and 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, Chronicles and the Psalms, and the New Testament calls Jesus the Son of David.
Saint David of Wales (6th century), the patron saint of Wales, whose feast day is 1 March.
Dāwūd (داود), the form used in the Qur'an.
Dave and Davy are the most common English short forms.
